aws-emr:aws-glue-catalog:v2.notes: The Glue Data Catalog is how EMR Serverless reaches S3 Tables: the table bucket is mounted as the federated s3tablescatalog and addressed with catalog-impl=GlueCatalog plus glue.id=<account>:s3tablescatalog/<bucket>. Measured: namespace and table creation, insert, row-level update, read, and drop.
caveats: Requires the table bucket to be integrated with AWS analytics services, which creates the s3tablescatalog federated catalog.

A warehouse must still be configured even though it is never written to. GlueCatalog derives a table location on the client and rejects an empty warehouse, while S3 Tables overrides it with a service-managed location.
The native S3TablesCatalog client is not usable from EMR Serverless without VPC access: it calls s3tables.<region>.amazonaws.com directly, which the default EMR network cannot route to.

caveats: S3 Tables-side documentation does not yet explicitly document VARIANT type support

aws-emr:shredded-variant:v3.notes: Not supported on EMR 8.0 / Spark 4.0.x. Spark 4.0 introduces the VARIANT data type, but its writer does not produce shredded variants (the Parquet typed/shredded variant encoding that stores common nested fields as real columns for pruning and predicate pushdown); VARIANT values are written as unshredded binary. Shredded-variant writing arrives with newer Spark and Parquet releases, not the Spark 4.0.2 bundled in EMR 8.0.
caveats: VARIANT columns themselves work (see variant-type); only the shredded storage layout is missing
Engine-side limitation: applies regardless of catalog, including S3 Tables

aws-emr:geometry-type:v3.notes: Measured on emr-spark-8.0.0 (Spark 4.0.2-amzn-0, Iceberg 1.10.1-amzn-0) against S3 Tables through the federated s3tablescatalog: CREATE TABLE with GEOMETRY(4326) and GEOGRAPHY(4326) columns is rejected with UNSUPPORTED_DATATYPE. Measured with spark.sql.geospatial.enabled set, so this is the runtime lacking the types rather than the session gating them. Glue 6.0 accepts the same DDL, which again puts the difference in the Spark build rather than in Iceberg.
caveats: Measured with the geospatial flag enabled, so it is not the session gate that refused.

aws-emr:nanosecond-timestamps:v3.notes: Measured on emr-spark-8.0.0 (Spark 4.0.2-amzn-0, Iceberg 1.10.1-amzn-0) against S3 Tables through the federated s3tablescatalog: both spellings are rejected with UNSUPPORTED_DATATYPE -- the Iceberg spec name TIMESTAMP_NS and Spark's parameterised TIMESTAMP_NTZ(9). The level is unchanged, but it is now measured rather than inferred from open-source Spark. Worth contrasting with Glue 6.0, where TIMESTAMP_NTZ(9) works: AWS added parameterised timestamp precision in the Spark 4.1.1 build Glue 6.0 ships, and EMR's Spark 4.0.2 build does not have it. So this is a runtime-version gap, not an Iceberg one.
caveats: Expected to change if an EMR release ships the Spark build that Glue 6.0 uses.

aws-emr:lineage:v3.notes: EMR 8.0 / Spark 4.0.2 supports Iceberg V3 row lineage with `_row_id` and `_last_updated_sequence_number` metadata fields for row-level change tracking; the engine-side capability applies regardless of catalog.
caveats: S3 Tables-side documentation does not yet explicitly document lineage support

aws-emr:snowflake-horizon-catalog:v2.notes: EMR Spark natively supports the Iceberg REST catalog spec via iceberg-spark-runtime. Configure with spark.sql.catalog.<name>.type=rest pointing to the Horizon Catalog endpoint. Direct REST catalog connections support both reads and writes. Note: when routing through AWS Glue Catalog Federation, writes are not supported — that is a Glue/EMR federation path limitation, not an OSS Spark or Horizon Catalog limitation.
caveats: Write via direct REST catalog API is supported
Write via Glue Catalog Federation path is not supported (Glue engine limitation)

aws-emr:unknown-type:v3.notes: Measured on emr-spark-8.0.0 (Spark 4.0.2-amzn-0, Iceberg 1.10.1-amzn-0) against S3 Tables through the federated s3tablescatalog: declared as VOID, which is how Spark spells the Iceberg V3 unknown type. A row was written and read back with the column null, which is the whole behaviour of the type -- it holds only nulls and is never written to data files.
caveats: Spark's spelling is required: the Iceberg spec name UNKNOWN is rejected and only VOID is accepted.
Promotion of an unknown column to a concrete type later was not exercised; only declaration, write and read were measured.

aws-emr:google-lakehouse:v2.notes: Google Lakehouse exposes a standard Iceberg REST catalog, and this engine speaks the Iceberg REST Catalog protocol, so it can attach to the Google Lakehouse runtime catalog and read/write its tables like any other IRC endpoint. caveats: Inferred from generic Iceberg REST catalog support; not measured against Google Lakehouse specifically
